spec.definition: Inflation is the general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money over time.

prediction.prompt: Prices rise 3% every year for 30 years. What percent of today's buying power does a dollar kept in a drawer still have?

extremes.watch: At 1% inflation, purchasing power stays much higher after 30 years.
At 8% inflation, purchasing power is nearly wiped out within 30 years.

misconceptions.label: Lose 3 points a year
misconceptions.why_tempting: 3% a year for 30 years sounds like 90% lost.
misconceptions.refutation: Each year takes 3% of what's left, so the losses shrink: 1/1.03^30 = 41%.
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified

misconceptions.label: Small inflation doesn't add up
misconceptions.why_tempting: 3% a year feels too small to matter.
misconceptions.refutation: Over 30 years 3% a year removes more than half of a dollar's buying power.
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified
